subject: botany_2
question_text: In the wake of transpirational loss, why are C4 plants more efficient than C3 plants?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.39, printed question 59. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: The number is the answer. "Half as much water for the same carbon dioxide fixed" is what makes this an efficiency answer rather than a general statement.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Less water lost
steps.margin_note: Say what is saved and what is gained. Three lines.
lines: So they can fix more carbon dioxide than C3
plants for the same amount of water.
steps.why: Efficiency here means carbon gained per unit of water lost, so the answer has to compare the two quantities and not just say C4 plants are better.
common_mistakes: Saying C4 plants photosynthesise faster. The question is about WATER, not speed.
Giving no comparison at all. The word 'efficient' asks for a ratio.
steps.memory_tip: Efficiency is carbon gained for water spent.

steps.label: The measured comparison
steps.margin_note: One line with the figure in it. Box it.

lines.text: Half the water for the same carbon fixed

lines: A C4 plant loses only HALF as much water as a
C3 plant for the same amount of carbon dioxide
steps.why: A single figure settles the comparison, and it is the line an examiner can mark without reading the rest of the answer.
common_mistakes: Leaving the number out. 'Half' is the mark.
Writing twice as much. C4 plants lose HALF, not double.
